definition: Encog is a machine learning framework available for Java and .Net.
details: Encog supports different learning algorithms such as Bayesian Networks, Hidden Markov Models and Support Vector Machines. However, its main strength lies in its neural network algorithms. Encog contains classes to create a wide variety of networks, as well as support classes to normalize and process data for these neural networks. Encog trains using many different techniques. Multithreading is used to allow optimal training performance on multicore machines. Encog can be used for many tasks, including medical and financial research. A GUI based workbench is also provided to help model and train neural networks. Encog has been in active development since 2008.

explainer.lead: Encog is a machine learning framework for Java and .NET, with a particular focus on neural networks. It gives developers tools to prepare data, build models, and train them, including a graphical workbench for neural-network work.

tiers.eli5: Encog is like a toolbox for teaching computer programs to find patterns in information. It helps clean up the information, build a neural network, and practice with examples until the network is trained. It can also use several parts of a computer at once to make training faster.
tiers.practitioner: In Java or .NET, Encog provides classes for data normalization and processing, network construction, and training. Developers can use multithreaded training on multicore machines or model and train neural networks through the GUI workbench. The main practical considerations are preparing the data appropriately and selecting a suitable model and training technique.
tiers.paperLevel: Encog is a software framework implementing multiple machine learning methods, including Bayesian networks, hidden Markov models, support vector machines, and neural networks, with neural networks as its principal strength. In general terms, training maps a prepared dataset D and model parameters theta to updated parameters theta' using a selected training technique. Its multithreaded implementation targets training performance on multicore hardware; the objective and update rule depend on the chosen algorithm.

explainer.example: For a medical research dataset, a developer could normalize the input values, create a neural network with Encog's classes, and train it using multithreading on a multicore machine. The same modelling and training process could also be carried out with the graphical workbench.

usedIn.name: Medical research
usedIn.detail: Encog can be used to prepare research data and train machine learning models for medical tasks.

usedIn.name: Financial research
usedIn.detail: Its neural-network and other learning algorithms can be applied to financial data analysis and modelling.

explainer.intuition: Encog handles the recurring plumbing of a machine learning project: getting data into a usable form, choosing a model, and running training. Its broadest toolkit is for neural networks, although it also supports several other kinds of learning algorithms.
howItWorks: Load data and use Encog's support classes to normalize and process it.
Create a neural network or select another supported learning algorithm.
Choose a training technique and fit the model to the prepared data.
Use multithreading to take advantage of multicore machines during training.
Use the GUI workbench when modelling and training a neural network visually.
explainer.whyItMatters: It brings data preparation, model construction, and varied training methods into one framework for Java and .NET developers. Multicore training support and the workbench make neural-network experimentation more accessible without removing the option to work directly with classes.
misconceptions: Encog is not a single neural-network algorithm; it is a framework containing many models and training techniques.
It is not limited to neural networks, since it also supports Bayesian networks, hidden Markov models, and support vector machines.
The workbench is not the only way to use it; developers can work with its classes directly.
